claims.text: The solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is a single-phase equiatomic solid solution.
The as-solidified alloy has a homogeneous elemental distribution.
Mobile solute atoms temporarily pin dislocations in this alloy.
Temporary solute pinning produces dynamic strain aging.
Dynamic strain aging causes serrated stress-strain flow in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Intermediate temperatures and strain rates increase solute mobility sufficiently to enable dynamic strain aging.
Serrated flow caused by dynamic strain aging leads to an inverse Hall-Petch effect.
Relative to the baseline, intermediate conditions will produce a pronounced serrated stress-strain response.
Relative to the baseline, intermediate conditions will reduce the alloy's yield strength.
A reduction in yield strength with changing temperature or strain rate is indicative of inverse Hall-Petch behavior.
At the proposed room-temperature, low-strain-rate baseline, solute mobility and dynamic strain aging are negligible.
The proposed effect occurs only in temperature and strain-rate regimes permitting sufficient solute mobility.
Outside the dynamic-strain-aging regime, traditional strengthening mechanisms dominate.
Comparison with a Co-containing variant can assess whether the behavior is specifically attributable to solute-driven dynamic strain aging in the Co-free alloy.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis labels a temperature- or strain-rate-dependent yield-strength reduction as an inverse Hall-Petch effect, but inverse Hall-Petch behavior is a grain-size dependence. The proposed controlled variables are temperature and strain rate, while grain size is only measured after deformation and is not systematically varied, so the named outcome is not operationally tested.
